audit.report: Checkout degraded to 43% success when the refund_batch_settle job (pid 1300806) held an idle transaction open for 4.2s, blocking 12 sessions. Both guardians agreed in a single round to WAIT for the blocker to complete because it is a PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT workload with a never_interrupt policy and non-replayable status, and the tradeoff analysis showed its ~41s remaining runtime would cost ~$7,109 in lost checkout revenue but still fit within the 60s degradation tolerance. The blocker finished on its own after 0s of waiting. Verification confirmed full recovery: checkout success reached 100% (36/36 over 10s), no lock waits remained, and no protected settlements were aborted.
audit.root_cause: The refund_batch_settle job entered an idle-in-transaction state (last statement SELECT 1) for 4.2s, acquiring locks that blocked all checkout sessions and degraded success to 43%.
lessons: For refund_batch_settle: Add proactive monitoring of transaction idle time on settlement_worker since this PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT workload has a never_interrupt policy — any idle-in-transaction state immediately blocks checkout and cannot be terminated.

For refund_batch_settle: Implement a pre-flight check for long-running transactions before the batch starts, because its typical 45s runtime leaves only ~15s margin against the 60s business degradation tolerance.

For refund_batch_settle: Instrument settlement_worker to emit heartbeat/progress metrics so guardians can distinguish 'stuck' from 'slow but progressing' without needing to probe workload registry during an incident.
audit.negotiation_critique: Database guardian correctly gathered evidence (workload registry, tradeoff, protected settlements) before proposing; continuity guardian accepted immediately because waiting fit within the 60s tolerance and terminating would violate invariant I1 (never_interrupt for PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT). No rounds were wasted — pact agreed in 1 round.
follow_ups: Add transaction idle timeout alerting for settlement_worker/refund_batch_settle at 30s (half the 60s business tolerance) to catch idle-in-transaction states before they breach SLO.
Review refund_batch_settle code for the SELECT 1 idle-in-transaction pattern and add explicit commit/rollback boundaries to prevent lock hold during idle periods.
Document the $7,109 wait-cost vs. never_interrupt invariant tradeoff in the incident response playbook for payments-core team.
